summary: Montreal Mirabel International Airport (YMX/CYMX) opened in 1975 as Canada's ambitious mega-hub and was once the world's largest airport by land area. Located about 60 km northwest of Montréal in Mirabel, Quebec, it lost scheduled passenger service in 2004 and now functions mainly as a cargo, aerospace, and general aviation airport. Its vast, partially unused site and iconic futuristic terminal remain distinctive features of Canadian aviation history.
faqs:
Q: Does Montreal Mirabel (YMX) have scheduled passenger flights?
A: No. Scheduled passenger service ended in 2004, and passenger flights now use Montréal-Trudeau International Airport (YUL).

Q: What is YMX used for today?
A: It primarily supports cargo operations, general and business aviation, aerospace manufacturing, maintenance, flight training, and some film production.

Q: How far is Mirabel from downtown Montréal?
A: It is about 60 km (37 mi) northwest of downtown Montréal, typically a 45–60 minute drive by car depending on traffic.

Q: Can I arrange public transit to YMX?
A: Public transit options are very limited and not practical for most visitors; a car, taxi, or pre-arranged shuttle is strongly recommended.
transport_tips: YMX is not served by frequent public transit; most travelers arrive by car via Autoroute 15 north from Montréal, a drive of roughly 45–60 minutes depending on traffic. Taxis and rideshares are limited, so pre-book ground transport or confirm pickup with your cargo/private flight operator. If you're connecting to Montréal-Trudeau (YUL) for passenger flights, allow extra time because the airports are on opposite sides of the city.
local_tip: The airport is enormous and facilities are spread out; if you're visiting for cargo, maintenance, or an aerospace event, confirm the exact building/gate in advance and drive between them rather than expecting to walk.
